effect.purpose: Read-only Effect v4 source pinned to the tag matching the installed effect release — the authority on what v4 actually exports, plus the v3→v4 migration notes.

effected.purpose: Read-only source for @effected/github-actions, @effected/github and @effected/jsonc — the libraries this action is built on. Pin tracks the installed @effected/github-actions version.

notes.note: `git -C .repos/effected describe --tags` reports `@effected/app@0.14.0`, NOT the `@effected/github-actions@0.11.0` this entry is pinned to. That is not drift — `describe` picks the nearest reachable tag in a monorepo that tags per package, and many packages share a release commit. (It reported a sibling `@effected/app` tag at the previous 0.5.0 pin too, so this is the steady-state behavior, not a one-off.) Check the gitlink against `repos_inspect` or `git rev-parse HEAD` (expect `86f52f5`), never `describe`, before concluding the pin moved.

`.claude/design/marketplace-manager/architecture.md` (Decision D-2) cites this repo by LINE ANCHOR: `packages/github/src/GitBranch.ts:46-69`. Verified at this pin (`86f52f5`): line 46 is the `@remarks` opener, line 69 ends `on the bare target head.`, and `readonly upsert` follows at 71. The range did NOT move across the 0.5.0 -> 0.11.0 re-pin. Verify it with `grep -n '@remarks\|on the bare target head' <file>` and never by eyeballing a `sed -n 'A,Bp'` range — the first printed line is A, not the line you want, and an off-by-two there already produced one wrong "correction" to this anchor. It is the only line-number reference from our design docs into a vendored repo. The surrounding prose quotes the TSDoc's substance, so the doc stays correct either way; only the range can go stale and mislead. Re-check on any re-pin.
